solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The old man rises with very little desire to eat

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the words for the old man are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the old man is a familiar word for father, PA
petite means very small, dainty

explanation.surface: A father gets up hardly wanting anything to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is the natural wish or hunger for food, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: short tells us the musical note's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

explanation.surface: A memo about a brief skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note short skirt' reads as describing a miniskirt, but 'short' is the cut: MINIM docked of its last M. 'Note' looks like the definition but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a very short skirt, the everyday clipped form of miniskirt.

definitions.meaning: to issue something is to release or publish it
in cricket a batter dismissed is got out by the fielding side

explanation.surface: A matter that was thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a statement is to issue it, and a put-out batter has been dismissed in cricket.

indicators.note: across means the pair of sons stretches over and around the lake

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, twice
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Two boys race around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a verb for the sons, but it is the noun: a run of matches or episodes.
explanation.definitionFit: A run of games or wins is a sequence, a successive set of things.

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so the fellow comes after the idea

parts.note: a plan is an idea or scheme
gent is short for gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A loud chap backing a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, resonant and often mournful sound, close to noisy.

indicators.note: it's said marks that the word for food is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: fare is food and drink, as in simple fare

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the meal was passable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair can mean reasonable but not outstanding, as in a fair attempt: merely satisfactory.

indicators.note: to re-sort letters is to sort them again into a new order, read here as re-sort

explanation.surface: A present wrapped up at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort, the anagram signal for TIED UP AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift for something is a natural talent or flair, a synonym of aptitude.

definitions.meaning: the star of a show plays the principal role
a clue in a detective case is a pointer to follow up

explanation.definitionFit: The lead in a film is its star, and a lead in an investigation is a clue.

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are arranged into a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: Someone has bought in additional wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered in' looks like a shopping phrase, but 'Ordered' alone is the signal and 'in' joins 'more' as the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is a fine soft wool from the sheep breed of that name.

indicators.note: leaking means the champion's word lets a letter escape from it

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: The champion lets slip his wife's confidential matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'wife's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts or feelings are private ones, kept hidden from others.

indicators.note: right away is read as the abbreviation for right going away from the trick's word

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or ploy

explanation.surface: Use a dodge immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once', but it splits: R is taken away from RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a tool or method is to put it to work, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Name one foolish person, then another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
another foolish person, so another word of that sense, a twit

explanation.surface: Identify one idiot, then a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' borrows the definition: a second foolish person, TWIT, follows N and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly, stupid person, an informal term of abuse.

parts.note: with can mean along with, and

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for charge is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a ward is a person in someone's charge

explanation.surface: Retract something and then raise the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge up' reads as a price rise, but 'up' turns WARD into DRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw a remark is to retract it; to withdraw money is to take it back out.

indicators.note: outside means the agent's word wraps around the shelter's word

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
lee is shelter from the wind, as in the lee of a wall

explanation.surface: An exhausted spy stands outside a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy means drowsy, ready for sleep, close to weary.

clue.text: Exercises before first of several drinks

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word several

parts.note: to sup is to drink, so sups means drinks

explanation.surface: A workout before one starts on several drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESS-UPS are the British name for push-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Press-ups, push-ups elsewhere, are a standard floor exercise for the arms and chest.

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for studied is heard, not seen

parts.note: read, past tense, means studied, and is pronounced like the colour
top means first, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper is said to have studied something first.
explanation.walkthrough: A RED-TOP is a British tabloid, so called for the red masthead of papers like The Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-top is the British nickname for a popular tabloid newspaper, from its red title banner.

clue.text: Rather small-minded hiding last of cider

indicators.note: hiding means the petty word holds the letter concealed inside it

parts.note: petty means small-minded, mean-spirited

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word cider

explanation.surface: A rather mean person conceals the dregs of the cider.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty used as an adverb means fairly or somewhat, as in pretty good.

parts.note: un is the French for a, as a Parisian would say
a drawn match is tied, neither side winning

explanation.surface: A Parisian was freed after being sketched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' suggests a picture, but it is the sports sense: a draw is a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Untied means unbound, freed from ropes or knots, so let loose.

indicators.note: before places the university word ahead of the defeat word

parts.note: up means at university in British usage, as in up at Oxford
to beat is to defeat

explanation.surface: A student stays hopeful before a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Being UP is British for being in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An upbeat mood is cheerful and hopeful, a synonym of positive.

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words jumper I purchased

explanation.surface: A hole in the sweater I bought.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip is to tear, and a rip is a tear in cloth.

parts.note: P stands for piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: novel means new, so the word read is made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A military chaplain reads a novel softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being read, but it is the adjective meaning new, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal name for a chaplain in the armed forces.

clue.text: Fifty on board vessel providing storyline

indicators.note: on board means the fifty is carried inside the vessel word like cargo

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for holding things
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people aboard a ship make for a good story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' reads as a ship, but it is a container, POT.
explanation.definitionFit: The plot of a novel or film is its sequence of events, its narrative.

clue.text: Black parasitic insect does for garment

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a louse is a small parasitic insect

explanation.surface: A black parasite ruins a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does for' looks like 'destroys' but is only a link: the pieces make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouse is a woman's loose shirt, one particular item of clothing.

indicators.note: from is read as taking letters out of the word famous, leaving only its inner pair

explanation.surface: Evict someone from a well-known road.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter slip, as the Times for the Times blog notes: the setter meant the answer to run inside famous street, but that run has one S too many.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to expel them or drive them from a position.

clue.text: Old garment, article obtained in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
got means obtained

explanation.surface: An ancient piece of clothing was picked up during an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks economic but means going back.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Complex patterns in part of church

indicators.note: complex means intricate or involved, so the word patterns is jumbled up

explanation.surface: Intricate designs in a section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the cross arm of a cruciform church, crossing the nave.
